label: input w or r during the original phase (history-gated)
explanation: Fires only in the original (input) phase, almost always at t=1..8 (never t=0, the delimiter step, or the copy phase apart from 9 stray steps). It is token-selective: input w or r carries about 83% of the activation mass (w 42%, r 40%). Weaker secondary tokens are l, x, e, k (about 16% of mass together), with traces on z and n. It is strongly history-gated: only about 26% of w/r inputs at t>=1 fire. Firing is more likely and stronger when the sequence starts with j, 3, p, f, i, u, 1 or d. With first_tok in that set, precision on w/r rises to 0.50, and those steps hold about 52% of the mass while making up 37% of the active steps. First occurrences dominate (92% of mass has in_first=1). Activity peaks at t=2..4. I could not find a simple prefix-set rule that predicts which w/r steps fire, so precision stays low.
